text: On Harry Frankfurt's hierarchical (mesh) theory, an agent has freedom of the will when which condition holds?
choices: Her action is undetermined by any prior state.
Her action-producing mechanism is moderately reasons-responsive.
She could have chosen otherwise given the actual past and laws.
The first-order desire that actually moves her is one she wants to be moved by, in accord with her second-order volition.
explanation: Frankfurt locates freedom of will in a mesh between levels: having the effective first-order desire one wants to have, endorsed by a second-order volition; the unwilling addict lacks this mesh. Reasons-responsiveness is Fischer and Ravizza's criterion, and the 'could have chosen otherwise' and 'undetermined' options are exactly what Frankfurt's compatibilism denies are required.
